rationale: Twenty-first pass, persistence mechanism. While checking whether a conflicting append can leave previously persisted entries reported as saved, the accounting in inMemory.merge turned out to cover all three cases: a plain append leaves savedTo alone, an append that starts at or below the marker resets savedTo to firstNewIndex-1, and a middle replacement lowers savedTo to at most firstNewIndex-1. That makes entriesToSave the set of entries not yet acknowledged as saved after truncation, which is the property a duplicate-avoidance or lost-persistence defect would violate. Recording it as a behaviour entry so later persistence work can rely on the invariant instead of re-deriving it.

knowledge.statement: inMemory.merge keeps the saved index consistent with truncation: a pure append leaves savedTo unchanged, an append whose first index is at or below the marker replaces the entries and sets savedTo to firstNewIndex-1, and a middle replacement keeps savedTo at min(savedTo, firstNewIndex-1). entriesToSave then returns entries from savedTo+1 onward, so entries removed by a conflicting append are re-reported as not yet saved rather than being treated as already persisted.
knowledge.conditions: A follower appends or replaces raft entries, and the node later commits an Update whose StableLogTo acknowledges persisted entries.
